title: César Tralli: the million‑dollar salary driving online searches
seoTitle: César Tralli: million-dollar salary drives online searches
subtitle: Since joining Jornal Nacional, the journalist's compensation has become one of the most talked‑about topics.
excerpt: César Tralli's rise at Rede Globo, highlighted by the disclosure of his salary and contract, sparked huge public interest.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The recent disclosure of César Tralli's salary at Rede Globo, after his arrival on the Jornal Nacional desk in November 2025, catapulted the journalist into the online spotlight. The boost in his status and compensation at the network generated great interest, making him one of the most searched topics at the moment.

The rise at Rede Globo

Tralli's move to the Jornal Nacional desk marked a new phase in his Globo career, representing both a status and financial upgrade. According to research by Observatório na TV, his current remuneration is about R$ 350,000 per month, roughly R$ 4.2 million per year.

This amount is a substantial increase compared with the period when Tralli presented Jornal Hoje, when he earned about R$ 120,000 monthly. The R$ 230,000 monthly difference underscores the magnitude of this professional appreciation.

Career trajectory and professional recognition

With more than three decades at Rede Globo, César Tralli has covered daily news and special reports, presented Jornal Hoje and worked at GloboNews before assuming his current role. This experience, combined with credibility and confidence on camera, has turned him into one of the most valued names in television journalism.

The journalist is praised for the way he conducts his work, handling politics, economics and everyday topics with rigor while maintaining an accessible language for the audience. In newsrooms and special coverage, he shows quickness in reorganizing information that arrives during the broadcast, keeping accuracy under pressure and mastering improvisation.

Contract details and salary comparisons

Advertising‑market sources say César Tralli has a contract with Globo until 2030. This long‑term link reinforces his importance within the company's structure and shows the trust placed in a communicator who can blend traditional newscasting with a direct conversation with viewers.

Despite the high figure, Tralli's salary still falls below the level reached by William Bonner. The presenter, after more than 40 years among the leading figures of national journalism, earned about R$ 900,000 per month for anchoring the newscast.

The formula for on‑screen success

César Tralli's ability to make complex topics in politics, economics and daily life understandable, coupled with his closeness to the audience, helped build the professional profile that underpins his position. His valuation reflects a blend of journalistic rigor and effective communication, traits that keep him prominent in Brazil's television landscape.

Information sourced from Terra, O TEMPO, NaTelinha.
